newsitem.title: SPAIN: EU approves Spain Telefonica-Unisource alliance.
newsitem.headline: EU approves Spain Telefonica-Unisource alliance.

text.p: The European Community has approved an alliance of Spain's Telefonica and Unisource after Spain promised to liberalise its telecommunications market, Development Minister Arias Salgado said on Saturday.

The commission had held up approval of the alliance which groups telecoms operators Dutch PTT, Telia AB of Sweden and Swiss Telecom PTT with Telefonica until Spain agreed to open its telecoms sector to free competition.

Salgado, in a written statement, called it a "good accord for the productivity of the country" adding the pact would also benefit partly state-owned Telefonica by allowing the international alliance to go forward.
He said the European Commission had accepted the date of December 1, 1998 for effective full liberalisation of the Spanish market. The deal was reached late on Friday.
The objective of the agreement was to achieve the full liberalisation of the market and allow Spain to incorporate the latest technology in telecommunications, Salgado said.
The Unisource deal is designed to take advantage of the break-up of national monopolies in Europe as well as to offer value-added services on a global scale.
Unisource was waiting for approval of the alliance to conclude a joint venture with U.S. AT&T to offer service on a global and not just European level.
